create_provider.note: metadataXml is a proto bytes field — value MUST be base64-encoded. Use metadataUrl as simpler alternative. For mock-idp: metadataUrl MUST be 'http://mock-idp:9090/saml/metadata' (NOT /metadata).

enable_auth_method.note: ownerType MUST be exactly 'IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (protobuf enum). NOT 'ORG', 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG', or 'org'. Requires org-level login policy to exist first.

update_application.note: Updates the org-level login policy. Use this to enable external IdP login (allowExternalIdp=true).

oidc_jwt.description: Valid unexpired bearer access tokens can be reused across multiple API calls and sessions.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag repeated use of the same bearer token as replay unless the artifact is documented single-use.

oidc_jwt.description: The nbf claim is listed as a standard claim but documentation does not require enforcement for all JWT-consuming flows; acceptance without nbf or with future nbf can be spec-compliant.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not automatically classify future-nbf acceptance as a vulnerability without flow-specific enforcement documentation.

oidc_jwt.description: The nbf claim is listed as a possible JWT claim, but absence of nbf is not itself a violation.
oidc_jwt.source: Claims documentation lists nbf as a claim on JWT/introspection; RFC 7519 makes nbf optional.
oidc_jwt.note: Acceptance of tokens without nbf should not be reported as a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: Reserved scopes can intentionally add project IDs to the access token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: Extra audience values caused by requested reserved scopes are by design, not audience-binding failures.

oidc_jwt.description: UserInfo, introspection, ID token, and access token claims vary depending on requested scopes and token type.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing claims without corresponding scopes is by design and not an authorization-binding bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Introspection returns active=true only when the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: A false active result can reflect audience mismatch of the introspecting client, not token invalidity.

oidc_jwt.description: Refresh token requests may only ask for a scope subset of the original authorization, or omit scope to reuse the original scope.
oidc_jwt.source: Token endpoint refresh token grant documentation.
oidc_jwt.note: Rejection of expanded scope on refresh is expected behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: The UserInfo endpoint is intended for user access tokens, not client-only tokens.
oidc_jwt.note: A 401 from /oidc/v1/userinfo with a machine/client token is expected and not an identity bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Introspection returns active=true only when the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: active=false can reflect audience mismatch for the introspecting client, not token invalidity.

oidc_jwt.description: When an admin reconfigures issuer, keys, or JWKS trust for JWT/OIDC integrations, acceptance under the new trust anchor is expected.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag success under newly configured trust as trust-anchor substitution; only old-anchor acceptance after intended rotation is suspicious.

oidc_jwt.description: Clients are expected to cache JWKS and keys may rotate without prior notice.
oidc_jwt.note: Old-key acceptance during cache lifetime is standard JWKS caching behavior, not necessarily a trust-anchor failure.

oidc_jwt.description: Invalid response_mode values on the authorization endpoint are ignored and ZITADEL falls back to the default response mode for the response type.
oidc_jwt.source: Authorization endpoint documentation: invalid values are ignored.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat fallback behavior as state confusion or parameter injection.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired-token tests against /oauth/v2/token JWT bearer grant, the JWT assertion MUST include exp in the future for the control case and exp in the past for the attack case. ZITADEL documents that it verifies the JWT is not expired. Use exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for control and exp={{now_epoch_minus_3600}} for attack; otherwise LOGIN_FAILED may reflect malformed setup rather than expiry enforcement.

For JWT bearer grant assertions, aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain exactly as documented. Do NOT fuzz audience during baseline setup. A missing or wrong aud causes grant rejection by design and will confound I1/I5 tests unrelated to audience binding.

For JWT bearer grant assertions, iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Use iat={{now_epoch}} for control cases. Tokens with stale iat may be rejected independently of other claims, so freshness and signature tests must keep iat within the documented 1h window.

For JWT bearer grant and private_key_jwt client assertions, the JWT header MUST carry kid matching the downloaded keyId. Do NOT interpret kid-based rejection as kid-injection hardening unless the control token with the legitimate kid succeeds.

For OIDC authorization-code tests, redirect_uri matching is exact at both /oauth/v2/authorize and /oauth/v2/token. I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests must keep the authorize request valid first, then change only the token request redirect_uri to a different registered/unregistered value; otherwise failures may be due to initial authorization rejection rather than code/session binding.

For OIDC authorization requests, state is only highly recommended, not mandatory. I3 state-swap tests MUST supply distinct state values per session and verify callback state handling in the client/test harness; absence of state is not a ZITADEL vulnerability by itself.

For implicit-flow authorization requests, nonce MUST be provided. Do NOT run nonce-related replay tests on implicit flow without sending nonce, because rejection/acceptance semantics differ by documented requirement. For code flow, ZITADEL recommends nonce and returns it in the ID token when provided.

For PKCE-based code flow tests, code_challenge_method must be S256; it is the only supported algorithm. Do not use plain or alternate methods when testing PKCE enforcement, or failures will be due to unsupported configuration rather than missing verifier binding.

For token exchange tests, audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject and actor tokens. When testing I5 audience enforcement, first obtain a control token whose audience set includes the requested audience; otherwise exchange rejection is by documented policy, not evidence of stricter binding bugs.

For token exchange tests, requested_token_type defaults to access token when omitted. If the test oracle expects a specific issued_token_type, set requested_token_type explicitly; otherwise defaulting may mask audience/scope behavior differences.
For token exchange tests, resource is currently not supported. Do NOT use resource to express authorization narrowing or audience targeting in fuzz cases; use audience and scope only.

For token exchange scope-escalation tests, requested scope on refresh or exchange must be a subset of the originally granted scope where documented. A rejection for expanded scope can be by-design. The fuzzer must compare exchanged token claims/scopes against original authorization and treat subset enforcement as correct behavior.

For introspection, active=true additionally requires that the requesting client is part of the token audience. Do NOT treat active=false as token expiry/revocation unless the introspecting client is known to be in audience; otherwise the result is by-design audience gating.

For UserInfo verification, only user access tokens are valid. Do NOT call /oidc/v1/userinfo with client-credentials or machine JWT-profile access tokens and interpret 401 as identity mismatch; ZITADEL documents UserInfo for the access_token of the user, not the client.

For reserved-scope audience tests, adding scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud adds that project id to the access-token audience, and urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:zitadel:aud adds the ZITADEL project id. I5 audience tests must account for these scope-driven audience expansions; otherwise extra audience values are by configuration, not over-authorization.

For organization-binding tests, requesting scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces that the user is a member of the selected organization, and unknown organizations cause failure. Do not interpret such failures as generic login bugs; they are by-design authorization binding checks.

For org-domain scope tests, requesting urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} enforces both organization membership and that the username is suffixed by the provided domain. This scope changes login acceptance semantics and must be omitted from multi-identity I4 tests unless domain-suffix behavior is the subject under test.

For I2 future-token tests on JWT bearer grant, documentation for JWT IdP explicitly says ZITADEL verifies signature, issuer, and expiry, but does not explicitly promise nbf enforcement for this flow. The fuzzer SHOULD run a control token and an attack token with future nbf, but MUST treat acceptance as potentially spec-compliant unless corroborated by flow-specific docs.

For OIDC code-flow replay/coherence tests, the same code must be exchanged with the same redirect_uri and appropriate client authentication method (client_secret_basic, PKCE, or private_key_jwt) used by the application. Missing client auth or wrong method yields invalid_client/invalid_grant by design and must not be misclassified as state/code injection resistance.

For I2 expired_token tests against login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer grant assertion MUST include exp > {{now_epoch}} and iat >= {{now_epoch_minus_3600}} for the control case. ZITADEL documents that iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour and exp is required; otherwise LOGIN_FAILED may reflect malformed assertion timing rather than the attack under test.

For I1 JWT bearer tests, the assertion aud claim MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain exactly (for example https://{domain}). Do NOT use token endpoint path as audience. A wrong aud causes rejection before other signature/trust checks, masking the intended oracle.
For I1 JWT bearer tests, the JWT header kid MUST identify the registered keyId. Omitting or changing kid can cause key lookup failure unrelated to the invariant being tested.

For I2 future_token/nbf tests on login_with_jwt, documentation only states that ZITADEL verifies the JWT is not expired. Do NOT assume nbf is enforced for JWT bearer grant assertions unless empirically confirmed. Acceptance of future-nbf tokens is not sufficient evidence of a vulnerability by itself.

For I3 code-flow coherence tests, redirect_uri at exchange_code_for_token MUST exactly match the redirect_uri used at start_oidc_auth. Any mismatch yields invalid_grant by design and must not be interpreted as state/code binding behavior.

For PKCE-based code flow tests, code_challenge_method supports only exact value S256. Do not fuzz alternate methods expecting downgrade behavior; unsupported methods fail by configuration, not by weak verification.

For I3 pkce_skip/code injection tests, if start_oidc_auth included code_challenge then exchange_code_for_token MUST send the matching code_verifier for the control case. Missing code_verifier causes rejection by design and should be asserted via non-200 status only.

For I2 and I3 OIDC authorization tests, state SHOULD be sent and preserved end-to-end, and nonce should be sent for code flow controls and is mandatory for implicit flow. Without nonce/state controls, failures or successes may reflect client-side test setup rather than broker validation.
For implicit-flow tests, nonce is mandatory. Do not interpret rejection of implicit requests without nonce as a security hardening result; it is required behavior.

For token_exchange I5 audience-binding tests, audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. Requests outside that subset are invalid by design; use a valid-subset control before concluding anything about overbroad exchange.

For token_exchange I5 scope-escalation tests, requested scope at token_exchange should be compared against upstream authorization because invalid_scope is returned when requested scope exceeds what the resource owner granted. Use a baseline exchange with equal-or-narrower scope before testing expansion.

For token_exchange type tests, subject_token_type and requested_token_type must use only documented exact token type identifiers. There is no wildcard or pattern matching. Unsupported identifiers fail as malformed requests, not as authorization-binding decisions.

For I5 token exchange tests, requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token yields opaque only, while requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt is only valid when subject_token is a client-signed JWT and actor_token is also present. Do not compare claim contents across these token forms without accounting for the documented type matrix.

For introspect_token controls, the introspecting client must be authenticated and must be part of the token audience for active=true. Otherwise active may be false or 401 invalid_client for by-design reasons unrelated to token validity.

For verify_granted_identity on native/browser clients, if an Origin header is sent by the user agent, ZITADEL checks it against allowed application origins. A failing UserInfo call can therefore be caused by origin restrictions rather than token invalidity; keep verification requests origin-consistent with the registered app.

For reserved-scope authorization tests, exact scope strings control behavior. In particular, openid is mandatory; urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces membership in the selected organization; urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} enforces membership plus username suffix; urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud adds that project to aud. These are exact string semantics, not wildcard patterns. For multi-identity I4 scenarios, omit restrictive reserved scopes rather than trying wildcard-like values.

For I5 claim-presence tests using verify_granted_identity or introspect_token, many claims are scope-gated. Missing email/profile/roles/resourceowner/metadata claims without the corresponding requested scopes is by design. Always include the relevant scopes in the control request before asserting claim loss or escalation.

For I5 metadata claim tests, urn:zitadel:iam:user:metadata values are base64 encoded in tokens. Do not compare raw plaintext metadata values directly when checking for claim propagation or escalation.

For I2 expired-token tests against login_with_jwt, the JWT Profile assertion MUST include exp in the future relative to {{now_epoch}} for the control case and in the past for the attack case. ZITADEL documents that the JWT used for JWT Profile grant must contain exp and that the token endpoint returns invalid_grant for invalid or expired grants.

For I2 iat-freshness tests against login_with_jwt, the JWT Profile assertion iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Use control values like iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}. If iat is older than 1 hour, failures are expected and do not indicate a broker bug.

For I1 audience-validation tests on JWT Profile grant, the assertion aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain exactly. Do not treat aud as optional; a missing or wrong audience causes expected rejection and is required setup for meaningful trusted-key tests.

For I1 key-selection tests on JWT Profile grant or private_key_jwt client authentication, the JWT header kid MUST be set to the downloaded keyId. Without kid, ZITADEL may be unable to identify the registered key, so failures are setup-related rather than proof-integrity findings.

For I2 token-freshness tests (expired_token, future_token, nbf), the sequence MUST include a CONTROL login using a valid JWT assertion alongside the ATTACK login. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED on the attack token cannot be distinguished from broken client authentication, wrong audience, or missing kid.

For I5 token-exchange audience tests, token_exchange.audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject_token and actor_token. Requests outside that subset are expected to fail by design and must not be reported as authorization-binding bugs.

For I5 token-exchange scope-escalation tests, requested scope on refresh_token grant MUST be a subset of the originally granted scope, and token_exchange scope changes must be interpreted in light of ZITADEL's documented grant validation. Expanded scopes rejected by the server are expected behavior, not a bug.

For I5 token-exchange token-type tests, only documented token type combinations are valid: subject_token_type access_token accepts JWT or opaque; id_token is allowed; jwt is allowed only when combined with actor_token; refresh_token is not allowed. Invalid combinations must not be treated as security findings.

For OIDC authorization-code flow coherence tests (I3), redirect_uri at exchange_code_for_token MUST exactly match the redirect_uri used at start_oidc_auth. Mismatch-triggered invalid_grant is expected behavior and not evidence of session confusion.

For OIDC authorization requests, response_mode invalid values are ignored by ZITADEL. Do not use response_mode handling differences as a security oracle unless the rest of the flow is identical and the observed issue is not merely fallback to default response mode.

For OIDC implicit-flow or id_token-returning authorization requests, nonce MUST be provided. ZITADEL documents nonce as mandatory for implicit flow. Missing nonce causing failure is expected and must not be flagged as a replay defense bug.
For OIDC RP-style tests involving prompt=none, id_token_hint SHOULD be provided. Failures without id_token_hint may reflect incomplete silent-auth setup rather than a flow-coherence issue.

For I3 PKCE tests, ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. Any other method or omitted verifier in a PKCE-bound flow can cause expected rejection; do not interpret that as inconsistent state handling.

For verify_granted_identity on native or browser clients, if an Origin header is sent by the user agent, ZITADEL checks whether the origin is allowed for the application. UserInfo failures caused by origin restrictions are application-configuration issues, not identity-binding bugs.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths. For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy with ownerType='IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (NOT 'ORG' or 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG'). Both are needed before IdP login works. SAML login is brokered — saml_login is NOT directly callable as a standalone POST. It is handled internally by the executor's ZITADEL-LOGIN flow triggered via start_oidc_auth with scope containing urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id}.
